items.claim: The row's second seam-evidence claim quotes a two-word call that does not stand in the verse it is attributed to, its digit belongs to a different object, and the stated ground for refusing the seam at that verse tests only for parent-level header shapes while the row's remaining bounding warrant is a tier-3 mark pair.
items.evidence: The pair בָּבֶ֜ל שְׂאוּ, carried under a byte-tier label and placed in apposition to the call standing at web:Jer.51.27, re-collates at tier none against oshb:Jer.51.27; it reaches byte tier only at oshb:Jer.51.12, and there בָּבֶ֜ל is the nomen rectum of the phrase governing the imperative, אֶל חוֹמֹ֨ת בָּבֶ֜ל שְׂאוּ נֵ֗ס (byte tier) -- so the pair splices the object of 'against the walls of' onto the verb and is not a call at either site. A skeleton sweep of that pair returns 1 verse (oshb:Jer.51.12 alone). The form the two verses actually share is שְׂאוּ נֵ֣ס, whose skeleton sweep returns 4 verses book-wide (oshb:Jer.4.6, oshb:Jer.50.2, oshb:Jer.51.12, oshb:Jer.51.27), 2 of them in this chapter: the cited chapter digit fits an object the row neither names nor quotes, and that shared call is skeleton-tier only across the pair (שְׂאוּ נֵ֗ס at oshb:Jer.51.12 against שְׂאוּ נֵ֣ס at oshb:Jer.51.27). Second arm: the row's own reading of oshb:Jer.51.27 as a discourse-imperative is byte-correct -- שְׂאוּ נֵ֣ס בָּאָ֗רֶץ תִּקְע֨וּ שׁוֹפָ֤ר בַּגּוֹיִם֙ (byte tier) opens a four-imperative series addressed to the nations in the plural, against the singular addressee of the mountain oracle at oshb:Jer.51.25, הִנְנִ֨י אֵלֶ֜יךָ הַ֤ר הַמַּשְׁחִית֙ (byte tier) -- yet the stated ground for holding the two together tests only for a koh-amar or word-event formula, which are the parent-level header shapes rather than the internal-seam classes; the imperative vocative at oshb:Jer.51.45 is allowed to open a unit on exactly the class denied here. What then bounds the row in its own prose is the flanking mark pair, setumah at MT 51:24 and MT 51:32 (single-witness, tier-3), which cannot drive a boundary in the Prophets; the byte-grade closure sitting at oshb:Jer.51.24, נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָֽה (byte tier) immediately before a fresh onset, is never cited.

items.claim: The koh-amar onset with the full divine-title stack, the five-note ketiv/qere opening of the following verse, and both flanking marks all verify at byte tier, and both cited digits are exact.
items.evidence: כֹ֨ה אָמַ֜ר יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל re-collates at byte tier against oshb:Jer.51.33, verse-initial after the causal particle, and the quoted bytes name the divine speaker themselves. A skeleton sweep of the koh-amar formula returns 4 verses in this chapter (oshb:Jer.51.1, oshb:Jer.51.33, oshb:Jer.51.36, oshb:Jer.51.58), so the onset is a real frame change and not one of the chapter's continuation clauses. The stacked title object sweeps to 32 verses book-wide at skeleton tier and oshb:Jer.51.33 is a member, matching the stated digit. The ketiv/qere engagement is byte-exact: oshb:Jer.51.34 opens אכלנו אֲכָלַ֣נִי (byte tier), the source serialising the unpointed ketiv immediately before the pointed qere, and the inventory records five notes on that verse -- the count the row gives, and the only K/Q verse anywhere in this cluster's span, so the disclosure symmetry is complete. Both flanking marks verify as setumah at MT 51:32 and MT 51:35 (single-witness, tier-3), the type claimed. Residual, not defects in substance: neither splice at oshb:Jer.51.34 carries a tier label, and the ketiv element quoted there is unpointed skeleton-grade material presented without that label.

items.claim: The tier-1 onset, the sleep-homograph ruling, the interior quotations, and the two-site digit all verify at byte tier; the only residual is a tier-3 absence argument in the rejected alternative.
items.evidence: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה re-collates at byte tier against oshb:Jer.51.36 and is verse-initial, one of the 4 koh-amar verses in this chapter (skeleton sweep of the formula: 4 verses -- oshb:Jer.51.1, oshb:Jer.51.33, oshb:Jer.51.36, oshb:Jer.51.58). וְיָשְׁנ֥וּ שְׁנַת עוֹלָ֖ם re-collates at byte tier against oshb:Jer.51.39 and, as the identical string, at byte tier again against oshb:Jer.51.57: the two verses carry the phrase under the same accentuation, so re-using one splice for both sites is byte-true rather than a copy degradation, and the stated two-verse chapter digit is exact (skeleton sweep of the construct phrase: 2 verses book-wide, both in this chapter). The homograph ruling is correct and correctly argued from the bytes: the middle word is the construct of the sleep noun, corroborated by וְלֹ֣א יָקִ֑יצוּ (byte tier) standing in both verses, and neither site is a year. אֵ֚יךְ נִלְכְּדָ֣ה שֵׁשַׁ֔ךְ re-collates at byte tier against oshb:Jer.51.41, and the Bel notice the row describes is byte-present verse-initially at oshb:Jer.51.44. Residual: the rejected alternative leans on the absence of an interior parashah mark across this stretch -- factually right, since the next mark after MT 51:35 is MT 51:51 -- as support for the rival reading, and states it without the single-witness disclosure the layer requires; mark absence is not evidence in either direction. The two paseq segs recorded at MT 51:37 inside the span go undisclosed, which the count-only status of that layer permits.

items.claim: The chapter-internal recurrence is asserted as near-verbatim with a byte-tier label in the same clause, but the two instances are byte-distinct and hold only at skeleton tier, and the formula is an eight-verse book-wide object cited with no digit.
items.evidence: לָכֵן֙ הִנֵּ֣ה יָמִ֣ים בָּאִ֔ים re-collates at byte tier against oshb:Jer.51.47, and לָכֵ֞ן הִנֵּֽה יָמִ֤ים בָּאִים֙ re-collates at byte tier against oshb:Jer.51.52; cross-collated, each reaches only skeleton tier at the other's ref. The consonantal skeletons are identical and every one of the four words differs in pointing or accent, so the recurrence is a skeleton-tier fact and cannot be near-verbatim in the bytes. The recurrence carries no tier of its own while a byte-tier label sits in the same clause on the splice beside it; that label proves the quote and not the relation, and the wording as written reads as a byte-level echo. No digit accompanies the claim either: a skeleton sweep of the formula returns 8 verses book-wide (oshb:Jer.7.32, oshb:Jer.16.14, oshb:Jer.19.6, oshb:Jer.23.7, oshb:Jer.48.12, oshb:Jer.49.2, oshb:Jer.51.47, oshb:Jer.51.52), two of them inside the same nations block, so presenting the pair as a chapter-internal echo understates the object. The rest of the row verifies and the seam itself stands: צְא֤וּ מִתּוֹכָהּ֙ עַמִּ֔י re-collates at byte tier against oshb:Jer.51.45 and is a genuine imperative-vocative onset of the internal-seam class; the year-token at oshb:Jer.51.46 is correctly withheld from the date class; the closing mark verifies as setumah at MT 51:51 (single-witness, tier-3).

items.claim: The row's opening warrant is a therefore-clause that belongs to none of the internal-seam classes and that the abutting material treats as row-internal at its other site, the sameness claim across the two sites is untiered and false in the bytes, and the two verses carrying the signature digit never enter the evidence refs.
items.evidence: The onset quoted for this seam, לָכֵ֞ן הִנֵּֽה יָמִ֤ים בָּאִים֙ (byte tier at oshb:Jer.51.52), is not a koh-amar -- a skeleton sweep of that formula returns 4 verses in this chapter (oshb:Jer.51.1, oshb:Jer.51.33, oshb:Jer.51.36, oshb:Jer.51.58), none of them this one -- and it is not a word-event header, a date frame, a vision opening, or an imperative. The identical formula five verses earlier, לָכֵן֙ הִנֵּ֣ה יָמִ֣ים בָּאִ֔ים (byte tier at oshb:Jer.51.47), is expressly read as row-internal in the material this row abuts, so one device opens a unit at one site and is denied that role at the other with no discriminator stated at either. Calling the two the same formula is also untiered and false at byte tier: cross-collation puts each at skeleton only against the other's ref. Separately, oshb:Jer.46.18 and oshb:Jer.48.15 carry the whole evidentiary weight of the signature digit and appear nowhere in the row's evidence refs. What does verify: נְאֻ֨ם הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמֽוֹ re-collates at byte tier against oshb:Jer.51.57 and a skeleton sweep of that stack returns exactly those 3 verses, so the digit and the distinction from a bare closure formula are right; the interior mark is properly disclosed and subordinated as setumah at MT 51:53 (single-witness, tier-3); and the rejected alternative's byte reading is correct, the verse after that mark opening ק֥וֹל זְעָקָ֖ה מִבָּבֶ֑ל (byte tier at oshb:Jer.51.54) with neither a koh-amar nor an imperative.

items.claim: The one-verse row's tier-1 onset and both flanking marks verify in the bytes and the inventory, and the row ranks the tiers in the only order the parashah layer permits.
items.evidence: כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת re-collates at byte tier against oshb:Jer.51.58 and stands verse-initial there; a skeleton sweep of the koh-amar formula returns 4 verses in this chapter (oshb:Jer.51.1, oshb:Jer.51.33, oshb:Jer.51.36, oshb:Jer.51.58), so this is a genuine fresh onset and not a continuation, and the quoted bytes name the divine speaker themselves. Both flanking marks verify as setumah under the claimed type at MT 51:57 and MT 51:58 (single-witness, tier-3) -- neither is petuchah, so the types are not conflated -- and the row states the ranking correctly, naming the marks as corroboration on top of the koh-amar onset rather than as the driver. The span uses the full X-X single-verse form, no K/Q note falls on this verse, and a one-verse unit admits no interior seam.

items.claim: The commission header, its internal date, the one-unit symbolic-act treatment, and the colophon terminus all verify at byte tier, and the header is correctly kept apart from the word-event shapes.
items.evidence: הַדָּבָ֞ר אֲשֶׁר צִוָּ֣ה יִרְמְיָ֣הוּ הַנָּבִ֗יא re-collates at byte tier against oshb:Jer.51.59 and stands verse-initial; the row rightly declines to call it a word-event formula, since its verb is the command verb and its subject is the prophet rather than the word, and it is equally distinct from the header shape opening the Babylon material at oshb:Jer.50.1. The date בִּשְׁנַ֥ת הָרְבִעִ֖ית לְמָלְכ֑וֹ re-collates at byte tier at the same ref and is header-internal exactly as described, and the row's separation of it from the noun standing at oshb:Jer.51.39 and oshb:Jer.51.57 is correct -- those two are the sleep homograph (skeleton sweep of the construct phrase: 2 verses book-wide) and this is a year. The one-unit treatment is byte-supportable: no koh-amar falls inside this span (skeleton sweep of the formula: 4 verses in this chapter, the last at oshb:Jer.51.58, immediately before the span), and no word-event or further date onset intervenes, so command, performance, and interpretation are separated by no internal-seam class. עַד הֵ֖נָּה דִּבְרֵ֥י יִרְמְיָֽהוּ re-collates at byte tier against oshb:Jer.51.64 and stands verse-final, and the closing mark verifies as setumah at MT 51:64 (single-witness, tier-3), so the terminus is byte-asserted as claimed and the row ends the parent exactly there, before the appendix. Residual, not defects in substance: the date splice is governed by a web: ref rather than its own oshb: ref and carries no tier label, though it does reach byte tier; and the English rendering attached to the header splice runs one word past the splice's extent.
